newsitem.title: USA: Tropicana sees major citrus losses from Fla freeze.
newsitem.headline: Tropicana sees major citrus losses from Fla freeze.

text.p: Tropicana, the nation's largest orange juice marketer, said the recent freeze in Florida will result in the worst crop losses in seven years.
It said between 10 million and 15 million 90-lb boxes of orange juice will be lost to freeze damage, or up to 7 percent of the Florida crop. The estimate includes both yields and fruit reduction.
Analysts said Tropicana's estimate could buoy frozen concentrated orange juice futures prices, on Friday.

"The market is probably going to react to this in a positive manner," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Whitter, said. "We have not seen this kind of figure coming from a major market mover like Tropicana."

But others said the overall impact will be negligible since the U.S. was expected to produce a record crop prior to the freeze, supplies from Brazil are readily available, and demand for orange juice remains weak.
"The damage will alleviate pressure from oversupply but not to the point where it will turn the market around," a Florida-based analyst said.
"Between Florida and Brazil, we have more than enough to meet demand."
The U.S. Department of Agriculture estimated the Florida crop at 220 million 90-lb boxes. It's next report, released Feb 12, will account for damages from the freeze.
Mark Gutsche, a spokesman for Tropicana, said it is too early to know whether the company will raise consumer prices for orange juice.
Tropicana Dole Beverages is a division of The Seagram Co Ltd.
